done.why: The world told me I'd used all 250 turns while I was heading down from the Temple with the torch, bell, book and candles. My last confirmed score was 125 of 350, and none of the temple loot made it to the trophy case.

about: It's a treasure hunt under a white house. You collect valuables and put them in a trophy case. Most of the action here is around Flood Control Dam #3 and the Frigid River: turn the bolt to drain the reservoir, dig the trunk out of the mud, pump up a magic boat and ride it down toward a waterfall. The world is strict about what you can carry, and it bends the old map in places. One stairway is now blocked by a cave-in, and the chimney fits only you, your lamp and one more thing.

moments.note: The troll died from one sword blow. My next three attack commands answered 'You can't see any such thing.'
The weight limit kicked in early: 'Your load is too heavy, the sword not least of it.' I ended up juggling items all game.
Turning the bolt with the wrench opened the sluice gates, and the reservoir really did drain into mud with a jewel trunk in it.
I had to leave the sword behind to lift the trunk. The game's own wording hinted at that, which I liked.
I grabbed the buoy as the river swept me past and got 'You notice something funny about the feel of the buoy.' An emerald was inside.
I launched from the Shore and tried to paddle west. The river took me over Aragain Falls and I died. The warnings were there, but I never found a way across, and I lost all my carried treasures.

The death message was fair and generous: plain things scattered around the house, valuables 'rolled into some dark corner in or under it', and the lamp put back by 'somebody tidy'. It gave me a puzzle to solve instead of just a penalty.
The chimney only takes you, your lamp and one more thing. Since the trap door gets barred, every treasure meant its own loop: cellar, gallery, studio, up the chimney.
I found the emerald waiting in the attic, which fit the 'dark corner in or under' hint.
The stairs up from the Atlantis Room ended at a fresh cave-in with a chalk arrow pointing back. A nice way to wall off a route.
Typing 'echo' in the Loud Room changed the acoustics so I could pick up the platinum bar.
I lost several turns typing directions from the Dome Room as if I were in the Engravings Cave. That was my mistake, but the room names in the replies are terse.
I hit the turn cap right after reaching the temple with four new items in hand. All those chimney loops had eaten my budget.

wished: I wished I could cross to the west bank by boat or find another way home from the Shore and Sandy Beach without going over the falls.
I wished the chimney could take more than one item. Or that I could unbar the trap door from below, so banking treasures didn't cost a full loop each.
I wished for more turns. I reached the temple with the torch, bell, book and candles and couldn't use any of them.
I wished I could try the rainbow without first knowing where to find what makes it solid.

lines.line: Your load is too heavy, the sword not least of it.
lines.why: It told me what to drop, and later I dropped exactly that to lift the trunk.

lines.line: You notice something funny about the feel of the buoy.
lines.why: It made me open the buoy. Small and satisfying.

lines.line: Your belongings, such as they were, have not come with you. The plain things are strewn about the forest and the fields around the house, anything of value has rolled into some dark corner in or under it, and somebody tidy has put the lamp back in the living room.
lines.why: It turned my death into a scavenger hunt, and it told me enough to find everything again.

lines.line: It is made, as rainbows are, of light and water vapor, and you can see the river through it.
lines.why: Good prose, and a clear hint that I couldn't walk on it yet.

lines.line: The chimney has room for you, your lamp and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
lines.why: This rule shaped the whole second half of my session.

lines.line: somebody has chalked an arrow on the rubble pointing back the way you came. You take the hint.
lines.why: A witty way to close off part of the old map.

fun.why: Draining the dam, grabbing the buoy, the echo trick and recovering my lost treasures after dying were all fun. The repeated chimney trips were a chore.

engagement.why: The score kept giving me a clear goal, and each new rule (weight, chimney, death scatter) changed how I planned. The trophy-case loops dragged in the middle.

difficulty.why: Puzzles had fair hints. My one death came from ignoring the falls warnings. The real squeeze was the carry limits against the turn cap, and that's what kept me at 125.

interestingness.why: The changes from the familiar game were real and well judged: the death that scatters your things, the one-item chimney, the cave-in with the chalk arrow, the sword's weight. They made me think instead of just retracing an old path.

prose.why: New lines like the rainbow, the death aftermath and the chalk arrow are wry and clear, and they fit the classic voice. Some replies are too terse, like plain room names on revisits.
